procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after the November PE.
Breathing back to baseline, climbs the school stairs without stopping. No chest pain. On apixaban 5 BID, no missed doses, no bleeding other than a bruise or two. Off levetiracetam since November without seizures; driving again.
DM/HTN: no issues. Reflux controlled.
Meds: apixaban 5 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: BP at goal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Calves soft, no swelling.
A/P
1. PE (travel-provoked), prior DVT — continue apixaban to complete about 6 months (through May), then we'll decide together about stopping. CBC today.
2. T2DM — A1c today.
3. HTN/ADPKD — BMP.
4. Meningioma s/p resection — seizure-free off levetiracetam.
Mammogram next month. RTC May.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis, compared with 2023 and 2024. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious findings.

events.reason: Shortness of breath and chest pain

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of heart
conditions.note: left atrial myxoma, 5 cm, attached to the interatrial septum

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis. No ischemic ST or T-wave changes.
reports.conclusion: Normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes.

reports.text: Left atrium: 5 cm mobile mass attached by a stalk to the interatrial septum, prolapsing toward the mitral orifice in diastole. Left ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function. Right heart normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: 5 cm mobile left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum, most consistent with atrial myxoma. Normal left ventricular systolic function.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — regional hospital
Date of visit: 05/17/2025 (Saturday)

CC: short of breath, left chest pain.
HPI: 55F with sudden shortness of breath this morning and left-sided chest pain that is worse lying flat. Three months of fevers on and off, some weight loss and general malaise, which she had put down to the end of the school year.
PMH: PE 11/2024 on apixaban, DVT 2021, right frontal meningioma resected 5/2024, stage IA vulvar SCC excised 12/2023, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, GERD/hiatal hernia, lichen sclerosus.
Meds: apixaban 5 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, clobetasol ointment.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 98, SpO2 94% on room air.
Exam: mild respiratory distress. Mid-diastolic murmur at the apex that gets louder when she rolls from supine to the left lateral decubitus position. Lungs clear. Neuro exam normal.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes. Troponin normal.
Bedside then formal TTE: 5 cm mobile mass in the left atrium attached to the interatrial septum.

Impression: left atrial mass, likely myxoma, explaining the dyspnea, positional symptoms, murmur and constitutional symptoms. Recent PE on apixaban; CT not repeated given the echo finding.
Plan: cardiology and cardiac surgery consulted. Admit. Hold apixaban for planned surgery. Blood cultures drawn.
Emergency Medicine

medications.reason: Held for cardiac surgery; 6-month course for travel-provoked PE complete, not resumed

reports.text: Specimen: left atrial mass with attached portion of interatrial septum, 5.1 cm. Gelatinous lobulated tissue composed of stellate myxoma cells in a myxoid stroma with hemorrhage. No malignancy. Septal margin free of lesion.
reports.conclusion: Cardiac myxoma, left atrium, completely excised.

reports.text: Postoperative study. No residual left atrial mass; septal patch intact without shunt. Left ventricle normal in size, LVEF 60%. Normal valve function. Trace pericardial effusion, expected after surgery.
reports.conclusion: No residual mass after myxoma excision. LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Cardiac Surgery, regional hospital
Admitted 05/17/2025   Discharged 05/26/2025

Diagnosis: left atrial myxoma.
Procedure 05/20/2025: median sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, excision of left atrial myxoma with resection of the septal attachment and pericardial patch repair.

Course: admitted from the ED. Apixaban held 72 hours before surgery. Blood cultures from the ED with no growth. Uncomplicated operation and recovery; extubated the same evening, chest tubes out day 2. Fevers stopped after surgery. Pathology: cardiac myxoma, completely excised. Post-op TTE 5/23: no residual mass, LVEF 60%.
Anticoagulation: she has completed six months of apixaban for a travel-related PE in 11/2024. After discussion with her, apixaban was not restarted.

Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment as needed. STOP apixaban.
Allergies: NKDA.
Sternal precautions: no lifting over 10 lb and no driving for 6 weeks.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery in 4 weeks, cardiology with a yearly echo, PCP in 1-2 weeks.
Cardiac Surgery

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 8 days after discharge. Partner with her.
5/17 ED for sudden dyspnea and positional L chest pain; TTE showed a 5 cm left atrial mass on the septum. Excised 5/20 via sternotomy, path cardiac myxoma, complete. Post-op echo EF 60%, no residual. Summary reviewed.
In hindsight the fevers, tiredness and weight loss since February were the myxoma; no fever since surgery, appetite back. Sternum sore with coughing, using a pillow to splint. Walking twice a day.
Apixaban stopped in hospital, six-month course for the PE done. We had planned to make that call in May anyway; agree with stopping.
Med rec: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: weight down about 4 kg from February. Afebrile. Sternotomy healing, edges together, no erythema or drainage, sternum stable. Heart regular, no murmur now. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. LA myxoma s/p excision — recovering as expected. Cardiac surgery f/u 6/24. Cardiology yearly echo.
2. Hx PE — off anticoagulation. Reviewed clot symptoms; travel precautions.
3. Weight loss — from the myxoma, should come back; recheck weight in September.
4. T2DM/HTN — BP higher than her usual today; recheck at the physical. CBC and BMP today.
School note: out through the end of the year, sternal precautions until early July.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Follow-up
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
CARDIAC SURGERY CLINIC
Date: 06/24/2025
Five weeks after median sternotomy and excision of a left atrial myxoma.
She is walking two miles a day, no fevers, no palpitations, no shortness of breath.
Medications: lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: sternotomy well healed and stable. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: lifting restrictions end at 6 weeks. May drive now. Myxoma surveillance with yearly echocardiography through cardiology. Discharged from our clinic.
Cardiac Surgery

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYN ONCOLOGY SURVEILLANCE VISIT
Date: 07/17/2025
Visit postponed from May while she recovered from cardiac surgery (left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025).
Vulva: occasional itch only, using clobetasol twice weekly. No sores or bleeding.
Medications: lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: excision site well healed. Lichen sclerosus stable with no new plaques, erosions or ulcers. No inguinal adenopathy.
Impression: no evidence of recurrent vulvar cancer, 19 months out.
Plan: next visit in 6 months; then alternate with her gynecologist yearly.
Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Return to work note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning, school starts back for teachers on the 25th and HR needs a note saying I'm cleared to return without restrictions after the heart surgery. The surgeon's office said to ask you. Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Return to work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Letter is attached and also in your documents tab. Cardiac surgery cleared you in June and your lifting limits ended in July, so no restrictions. See you at your physical on September 9.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Two weeks into the school year, energy good.
Since last physical: PE 11/2024 (apixaban x 6 months, done); left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025, echo EF 60% after; vulvar SCC surveillance NED in July. Meningioma resected 2024, seizure-free off levetiracetam.
Weight back up close to last year's. No fevers.
Optometry exam in July, no retinopathy (report on file).
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
PHQ-9 2.
Exam: BP at goal. Sternotomy and craniotomy scars healed. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Feet intact, pulses good.
A/P
- Preventive: flu + COVID at nurse visit in October. Mammogram March. Colonoscopy 2030. Pap/HPV 2024 negative.
- T2DM: A1c, microalbumin, CMP today.
- HTN/ADPKD: stable.
- Hx myxoma: cardiology yearly echo.
RTC January.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccines given, L and R deltoid. No contraindications on screening. VIS given. Tolerated well, left after 15 minutes.

conditions.label: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage from right middle cerebral artery

reports.text: Diffuse hyperdensity filling the basal cisterns and the interhemispheric fissure, consistent with acute subarachnoid blood. No intraparenchymal hematoma. No mass effect or midline shift. Postoperative changes of prior right frontotemporal craniotomy.
reports.conclusion: Acute diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage. No intraparenchymal hematoma or mass effect.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — regional hospital
Date of visit: 11/02/2025 (Sunday)

CC: collapse at home.
HPI: 55-year-old woman brought in by ambulance after her partner found her collapsed at home. Per partner, this morning she complained of a stiff neck and briefly saw double. History from partner; patient unable to give history.
PMH: right frontal meningioma resected 2024, left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025, PE 11/2024 (anticoagulation completed), DVT 2021, vulvar SCC excised 2023, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, GERD.
Meds (per partner and pharmacy record): lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, clobetasol ointment. Not on anticoagulants.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 178/100, HR 52.
Exam: drowsy and disoriented. Localizes to pain but does not follow commands. Pupils reactive; mild right ptosis. Moving all four limbs.
CT head without contrast: diffuse hyperdensity in the basal cisterns and interhemispheric fissure; no intraparenchymal hematoma, no mass effect.
Coags normal.

Impression: acute subarachnoid hemorrhage, presumed aneurysmal; family history of ruptured cerebral aneurysm and ADPKD noted.
Plan: neurosurgery and neurointerventional radiology at bedside. Blood pressure lowered per hemorrhage protocol. CTA head ordered. Admit to neuro ICU.
Emergency Medicine

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (60 mg) by mouth every 4 hours to complete 21 days (last dose 11/23/2025)

documents.title: Neurocritical Care Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurocritical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Neuroscience ICU / Neurosurgery, regional hospital
Admitted 11/02/2025   Discharged 11/17/2025

Principal diagnosis: aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured right middle cerebral artery aneurysm.

Course:
CTA head on arrival showed a 6 mm aneurysm at the right MCA bifurcation. Underwent endovascular coiling the same day (11/02) with complete occlusion of the aneurysm. Started on nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for a 21-day course. Monitored in the neuro ICU with serial neuro exams. Mental status improved steadily over the first week. Transferred to the floor on day 9. Worked with PT, OT and speech therapy.
At discharge: alert, oriented, following commands, speech fluent, strength full. Right ptosis improving. Walking independently.

Discharge medications:
- nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours through 11/23/2025 (new)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment as needed (unchanged)
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: no driving until cleared by neurosurgery. No heavy lifting or straining for 4 weeks. Outpatient PT and OT ordered. Return for severe headache, confusion, weakness or seizure.
Follow-up: neurointerventional clinic in 3-4 weeks; MR angiogram at 6 months. PCP within 1 week.
Neurosurgery / Neurocritical Care

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit three days after discharge. Here with her partner and her son, who drove up for the week.
11/2 collapse at home after a morning of neck stiffness and brief double vision. CT: diffuse SAH. CTA: 6 mm R MCA bifurcation aneurysm, coiled same day. 15 days in hospital, ICU then floor. Discharge summary reviewed with them.
Now: tired, naps in the afternoon, mild headache, improving. Right eyelid still a little droopy. Thinking clear per family. Taking nimodipine every 4 hours with phone alarms, son set up a chart; last dose 11/23.
Med rec: nimodipine 60 q4h (ends 11/23), lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA. Son has the list.
Exam: alert, oriented x3, conversant. Mild R ptosis. EOM full. Strength and gait normal. Groin puncture site healed. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.
A/P
1. Aneurysmal SAH s/p coiling — recovering. Neurointerventional f/u 12/11, MRA in 6 months. OT/PT started this week. No driving.
2. HTN — BP acceptable today on lisinopril/HCTZ with nimodipine; recheck at next visit.
3. T2DM — continue metformin.
4. Family history of ruptured aneurysm with ADPKD — already known to neurosurgery.
Medical leave from school through at least January; FMLA forms completed.
Call or message with any new headache, confusion or weakness. RTC 1 month.

documents.title: Neurointerventional Follow-up
documents.author: neurointerventional radiology
documents.body:
NEUROINTERVENTIONAL CLINIC NOTE
Date: 12/11/2025
Valerie Slattery, 55. Ruptured right MCA bifurcation aneurysm (6 mm) presenting with diffuse SAH 11/02/2025, treated with endovascular coiling the same day with complete occlusion. Completed 21 days of nimodipine.
She is doing well: energy improving, headaches rare, ptosis nearly gone. Doing outpatient OT twice weekly.
Medications: lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: alert and oriented, fluent speech, very slight right lid droop, extraocular movements full, strength normal, gait steady.
Plan: MRI brain with MR angiogram in June to check the coil mass; this will also serve as her yearly meningioma surveillance scan. May drive from January if she remains well.
Neurointerventional Radiology

documents.title: Return to work question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient called asking whether she can go back to teaching when school resumes after break. Neurointerventional cleared her to drive from January. Discussed with PCP: okay for a half-day schedule for the first two weeks, then full time if tolerated. Letter faxed to school HR. She will message if fatigue limits her.
